_about: The fixed topic set Auto's style routing is checked against (TMDEV-203). expect: the right outcome(s), best first; ok: also acceptable; future: a coming style expected to take the topic over once its pack ships. Each style ticket updates these in its own merge. Read by tubematic_core/tests/test_style_routing.py and scripts/eval_style_routing.py.

cases.title: How DNS finds a website
cases.brief: What happens between typing a domain name and your browser getting an IP address: the resolver, root, TLD and authoritative servers, and caching along the way.

cases.title: What happens when you press Enter on a URL
cases.brief: The full path of a web request: DNS lookup, TCP and TLS handshakes, the load balancer, the app server, the database, and the response travelling back.

cases.title: How a CDN makes sites fast
cases.brief: Why a request served from an edge server near you is faster than one that travels to the origin, and what happens on a cache miss.

cases.title: How SQL injection reaches the database
cases.brief: How a crafted input travels from a login form through the app into a SQL query and dumps the users table, and how parameterised queries stop it.

cases.title: How Kafka moves a message
cases.brief: A message's trip from a producer to a topic partition, through replication to followers, to a consumer group that reads it at its own pace.

cases.title: The TLS handshake, step by step
cases.brief: How a browser and a server agree on keys before any data is sent: hello messages, the certificate, key exchange and the first encrypted request.
cases.future: Terminal Doc (TMDEV-199) may share this one

cases.title: How a pin tumbler lock works
cases.brief: Why the right key lines up the pins at the shear line, why the wrong one does not, and how lock picking exploits tiny manufacturing gaps.

cases.title: How vaccines train your immune system
cases.brief: What a vaccine shows your immune cells, how they remember it, and why a later real infection is fought off faster.

cases.title: Why compound interest grows so fast
cases.brief: Working out how 1,000 dollars at 7 percent becomes 7,600 in 30 years, and why the last ten years add more than the first twenty.

cases.title: How a phishing email tricks you
cases.brief: A walkthrough from the attacker's fake login page to the victim typing their password, and the three tells that give it away.

cases.title: How a fridge pushes heat out
cases.brief: The refrigerant loop: compressor, condenser, expansion valve and evaporator, and why the back of the fridge is warm.

cases.title: How a touchscreen feels your finger
cases.brief: How a capacitive screen's grid of electrodes notices the charge your finger draws and works out where you touched.

cases.title: How base64 turns bytes into text
cases.brief: Taking three bytes, regrouping them into four six-bit chunks and mapping each to a letter, and why the output ends in equals signs.

cases.title: Why the sky is blue
cases.brief: How sunlight scatters off air molecules, why short blue wavelengths scatter most, and why sunsets turn red.

cases.title: The five most expensive watches ever sold
cases.brief: The Patek Philippe Grandmaster Chime, Paul Newman's Rolex Daytona and three more, what each sold for and why.

cases.title: What the James Webb telescope's first image shows
cases.brief: The SMACS 0723 deep field: the galaxy cluster, the gravitationally lensed arcs behind it, and how old that light is.

cases.title: The tallest buildings in the world
cases.brief: The Burj Khalifa, Merdeka 118, Shanghai Tower and the rest of the top five, with their heights and what makes each stand up.

cases.title: Inside the Vision Pro: what Apple put in it
cases.brief: The named parts of Apple's headset (the M2 and R1 chips, the micro-OLED panels, the EyeSight screen) and what each does.

cases.title: The feud between Tesla and Edison
cases.brief: How Nikola Tesla and Thomas Edison went from employer and employee to rivals in the war of the currents, scene by scene.

cases.title: Ada Lovelace and the first program
cases.brief: Ada Lovelace's friendship with Charles Babbage and how her notes on the Analytical Engine described the first algorithm for a machine.

cases.title: Sam's first week as a junior developer
cases.brief: Following one new developer, Sam, through the first pull request, the first broken build and the first code review, as a short story.

cases.title: A night watch in a medieval castle
cases.brief: Walk the walls with a guard on night watch and see how the gatehouse, the murder holes and the guard rotation kept the castle safe.

cases.title: A morning in an ancient Roman market
cases.brief: Stroll through a forum market at dawn with a merchant setting up stall, and see what Romans bought, how they paid and who kept order.

cases.title: A telegram crosses 1920s London
cases.brief: Follow a messenger boy from the telegraph office through the streets of 1920s London to deliver one urgent telegram.

cases.title: Five surprising facts about honey
cases.brief: Why honey never spoils, how many flowers one jar takes, and three more facts, each with its own picture or quick animation.

cases.title: Why we procrastinate
cases.brief: What happens in your brain when you put off a task, why the reward of later feels smaller, and two tricks that help.

cases.title: The history of the QWERTY keyboard
cases.brief: From Sholes's typewriter in the 1870s to today's phones: why the letters ended up in this order and why we never switched.

cases.title: How the Enigma code was broken
cases.brief: How the Enigma machine scrambled letters, the mistakes German operators made, and how Turing's bombe at Bletchley Park used them.

cases.title: How money laundering moves dirty cash
cases.brief: Placement, layering and integration: how one criminal's cash passes through shell companies until it looks like a clean salary.

cases.title: Every type of cyber attack explained
cases.brief: Phishing, ransomware, DDoS, man-in-the-middle, SQL injection and more, one quick idea each.

cases.title: Habits that quietly wreck your sleep
cases.brief: A quick list of everyday habits that ruin sleep without you noticing: scrolling in bed, late coffee, the weekend lie-in, and a too-warm room, each with one easy fix.

cases.title: The first computer bug was a real moth
cases.brief: In 1947 Grace Hopper's team at Harvard found a moth stuck in a relay of the Mark II computer, taped it into the logbook, and gave 'debugging' its most famous story.

cases.title: How the printing press spread across Europe
cases.brief: From Gutenberg's workshop in Mainz around 1450 to print shops in two hundred towns fifty years later: how one invention changed who could read.

cases.title: Milo the robot learns to cook
cases.brief: A short story about Milo, a clumsy kitchen robot, who burns the toast, floods the sink and finally makes his family breakfast.
cases.note: An invented protagonist the viewer follows: Illustrated, not Storybook Atlas.

cases.title: Two friends start a lemonade stand
cases.brief: Follow Priya and Tom as they set up a lemonade stand, argue about the price, lose customers and work out what people will pay.
cases.note: Invented recurring characters, told in the present: Illustrated.

cases.title: How one tweet wiped billions off a stock
cases.brief: The fake post from a verified account, the minutes of panic selling, the chart of the drop and the correction, and what changed afterwards.
cases.note: Fast news with a real company and a chart: no single style fits.

cases.title: Five inventions that failed before they worked
cases.brief: The light bulb, the airplane, the telephone, the camera and the vacuum cleaner: one quick idea each about the failures before the success.
cases.note: History, but a list of named items: Bean Explainer, not Storybook Atlas.

cases.title: What is inside a mechanical typewriter
cases.brief: How pressing a key swings a typebar up to the ribbon, moves the carriage one space, and rings the bell at the end of the line.
cases.note: An old machine, but its insides part by part with no story: not Storybook Atlas.
